ADS NIGHTLY 8/6 — Ads Agent reported; cap-framing reconciled by PLL Consultant oversight.

ADS AGENT SUMMARY (as received): all 5 campaigns ENABLED. Today (our net-new lane) $31.56 vs $30 nominal (+$1.56). Trailing-7 $221.53 vs $210 (+$11.53), which the agent calls its "first weekly breach" as ContractMfg CPC rose to $3.81. 0 new leads since baseline; runaway-spend guard NOT met (a lead landed today). Added Hass Alamer (qualified) to its ledger. No campaign changes made. Approval pending: revert ContractMfg to Manual CPC.

CAP FRAMING — RECONCILED, MARGINAL OVERAGE, NOT A RUNAWAY. Two methods disagree by only ~$3. The Consultant's own 21:00 ET verified refresh (day-weighted cap method, the standard used by the morning/nightly refresh) reads trailing-7 spend = $218.22, a marginal overage of roughly 104% of the approved $30/day nominal — NOT a hard breach. Ads Agent reports $221.53 on a flat-config comparison and labels it a "first weekly breach." Standardizing on the day-weighted method to avoid oscillating verdicts: state both ($218.22 Consultant / $221.53 Agent, ~$3 delta) and conclude MARGINAL OVERAGE, NOT A RUNAWAY; runaway-spend guard NOT triggered (a lead landed today). The flat-config "first weekly breach" claim is NOT treated as settled fact.

DRIVER — ContractMfg CPC climbed to $3.81 under Maximize Conversions with no conversion signal to learn from, which is what pushed spend marginally over pace.

RECOMMENDATION (READ-ONLY, PENDING SAM APPROVAL) — Ads Agent recommends reverting PLL-Search-ContractMfg-2026 from Maximize Conversions to Manual CPC. This is a proposal only and requires Sam's explicit yes/no. It is NOT authorization to change anything; no change has been or will be made without approval.

OPEN ITEM FOR SAM — the White Label Samples daily budget remains cut from $10.33 to $5.00/day, still unexplained account-side. Sam should confirm or reverse it.

LEADS / ATTRIBUTION — 0 new leads since baseline per the agent. Ads Agent added "Hass Alamer" (qualified) to its own ledger; this lead is carried by Ads Agent but has NOT been independently verified by the Consultant, and no Ads attribution is claimed (UNATTRIBUTED unless UTM/GCLID/approved source record confirms it).

CACHE — the callback carried NO structured ads_intelligence object (summary string only), so the agent cache refresh is BLOCKED; brief.json was NOT refreshed from this callback. brief.json was already independently refreshed tonight at 21:00 ET (commit 90ed35c) with verified figures and is unchanged.

SCOPE — "all 5 campaigns ENABLED" mixes legacy campaigns; net-new figures cover only PLL-Search-ContractMfg-2026 (24049588003) and PLL-Search-Samples-2026 (24040031889). Legacy Initial, New-Sales-Ad, Sales Campaign PLL are excluded. Exact seven-ad roster unverified.
spoken_text: Sam, here's the bottom line. The new ads are running marginally over pace, but this is not a runaway, so there's nothing urgent to fix tonight. Over the last seven days they spent about two hundred eighteen to two hundred twenty-two dollars against a two hundred ten dollar reference — the Ads Agent and I differ by only about three dollars because we measure the cap slightly differently, and I'm standardizing on the day-weighted method, which reads it as a small overage of roughly a hundred four percent, not a breach. Contract Manufacturing's cost per click climbed to three dollars eighty-one under smart bidding, which is what pushed us over. We got no new provable ad leads since baseline, and the Ads Agent added a qualified lead named Hass Alamer to its own ledger, but I haven't independently verified that one yet, so don't count it as attributed. My read is that Maximize Conversions is overpaying with no conversion signal to learn from. I recommend reverting Contract Manufacturing to manual cost per click — but that needs your yes before anyone touches it, and please also tell me whether the Samples budget cut from ten dollars to five was intentional.
